Playbook.name: Linux — Suspicious Kworker UID Elevation - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A process named like a kworker kernel thread changed session/UID (event.action session_id_change) to a different user - kernel threads never change UID, so this indicates a masquerading process performing privilege escalation.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A fake-kworker escalating UID is exploitation of the kernel or a masquerading rootkit gaining privilege.

Assets.AssetType: Linux servers (core banking, app, DB - INTDOM)

LogSources.LogSource: Linux auditd via Elastic Agent - logs-auditd.log-*, logs-auditd_manager.auditd-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Linux auditd (verified live). AVAILABLE fields: process.name, process.executable, user.name, host.name, event.action, event.category. NOT COLLECTED: process.args, process.command_line, process.parent.name, file.path. Linux FIM is not deployed (logs-fim.event-* holds only Windows paths). Investigation is therefore limited to process identity + acting user; argument/file-content and parent-chain confirmation must be done on the host.

Signal.Name: Kworker UID elevation
Signal.Details: auditd process/exec event matching kworker uid elevation (see telemetry note on field limits).

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Linux host where the activity occurred.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence; note auditd field limits (no args/file.path) - some confirmation must occur on the host.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the kworker uid elevation on $hostname is malicious, using available process/user evidence and host inspection.

Step.name: Confirm the process execution on the host and the acting user
Step.Purpose: Confirm the flagged process ran, on which host, by which user, and how often - the core evidence available from auditd.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-*,logs-auditd_manager.auditd-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.category == "process" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)kworker.*" AND event.action RLIKE "(?i).*session_id_change.*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), executables = VALUES(process.executable), users = VALUES(user.name), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A kworker-named process with a session_id_change to root/another user is masquerade + privilege change - real kworkers never do this. Note the users involved.

Step.name: Profile the acting user's process activity on the host
Step.Purpose: The acting user's broader process activity separates an interactive attacker/anomaly from a service/automation account.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-*,logs-auditd_manager.auditd-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.category == "process" AND user.name == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), processes = VALUES(process.name), execs = COUNT_DISTINCT(process.executable) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A root/service account running the flagged tool as part of automation differs from an interactive/unexpected user. Correlate the user with the host's role (DB/app server).

Node.Condition: A kworker-named process performing a UID/session change, especially to root.
Node.Result: True Positive (Malicious Activity - investigate on host, IR if confirmed)

Node.Condition: The process is run by a known service/automation account as part of the host's normal operation.
Behavior is consistent with a documented admin/maintenance action.
Process identity confirms the tool ran but argument/file context (not collected in auditd) is needed to decide, and host inspection is not yet available.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-LX-EXEC, INV-02-LX-USER to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate kernel thread (which never changes UID) - i.e. a false match.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the benign source/automation; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: A masquerading process escalating privilege under a kworker disguise.

SOCAction.Item: Inspect the host (full command line, files touched, parent process); isolate if confirmed malicious; open IR.
Reset credentials used on the host; hunt the same activity on peer hosts.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A container/namespacing artifact producing a kworker UID-change event.

Indicators.Item: A known containerization behavior confirmed benign.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Inspect the host for the full command line and file/parent context auditd did not capture.
If malicious indicators, isolate the host.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture the process tree and touched files on-host; open IR.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the technique; expand auditd to collect execve args and file paths (see QualityChecks).

QualityChecks.Check: AUDITD TELEMETRY GAP: process.args, process.command_line, process.parent.name and file.path are NOT collected in JCB auditd; Linux FIM is not deployed. RECOMMENDATION: enable the auditd execve/path rules and Linux FIM so argument- and file-based confirmation is available in-SIEM.
Tune known service/automation accounts via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Process attributed to known automation/admin; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host inspected and contained; technique eradicated; peers swept.
